properties.name: Anthony restated the fix-properly rule as the second half of root-cause, on seeing the word "patches" — and named the cost-of-change curve as the reason
properties.statement:
ANTHONY, 2026-09-07, in his own words: "it should also be a design rule, but as well as determining root cause, I like things to be fixed properly, even if it takes longer and requires more work. in the long run, we are better off served by putting the work in now. (this touches upon that it is more difficult to fix things down the road - we had a brainstorming session on this last session). when I see the word 'patches', it makes me worry that we are fixing the root cause and that we are also not fixing the issue properly."

WHAT IS NEW HERE, since the rule already existed and he had already made it permanent on 2026-08-17. Three things.

(1) HE COUPLED THE TWO RULES EXPLICITLY. Finding the cause and fixing at the cause are one sequence, not two independent disciplines: "as well as determining root cause". The root-cause skill's step 8 already points at this rule, but the two RULES were joined by nothing, so a reader of either met only half the doctrine. The edges drawn with this record close that.

(2) HE NAMED THE COST CURVE AS THE REASON, referring back to his own brainstorm of 2026-09-06 on the Cost of Change Curve and the Rule of Tens. That is the argument beneath clause 2 of the rule, and it means the parked cost-of-change instrument is not merely an interesting measure: it would put a number on the thing this rule asks people to believe.

(3) THE TRIGGER WAS A WORD, AND THE WORD WAS THE AGENT'S. He read "patched 25 literals" in a progress report and reasonably heard "worked around 25 problems". It meant mechanical edits to test-code struct literals - adding an explicit None for a newly added optional parameter so existing tests keep compiling - which is neither a fix nor a workaround. THE LESSON IS ABOUT REPORTING, NOT ABOUT THE WORK: a word that names a known anti-pattern must not be spent on something else, because the owner cannot audit every diff and is reading the words instead. The vocabulary is the interface.

WHAT THE AUDIT FOUND WHEN HE ASKED. The day's five changes were each taken at the cause rather than around it: a constructor for the moment a cause is written rather than a reminder to remember the skill; the reachability filter unfused rather than special-cased for the two reported properties; the tool-to-type map extended to every writer rather than to the one that leaked; six constructors given the parameter rather than the one reported; and a schema sweep as the test rather than a list of today's six.

WHAT IS HONESTLY DEFERRED, stated because this is exactly the record where hiding it would be the failure: 43 declared properties remain unreachable from the surface and are GRANDFATHERED into a baseline rather than fixed. Three node types - Actor, EnvironmentRule, QualityGate - have no typed constructor at all, so their properties cannot be given parameters without first deciding whether those types should be user-writable. Both are visible, counted and gated against growth; neither is fixed. Under clause 1 that is a decision to carry a cost, and it is the owner's to take rather than the agent's to leave unmentioned.
